about: The table simulator's rooms (docs/RAIL-PLAN.md R3.1). Every field says in 'sources' whether it is SOURCED (from the corpus or docs/research/hh-formats/), PARTLY SOURCED, or INVENTED. Window titles are all INVENTED: no real table title has been captured yet (sites.json tables.title is null until R3.3/R3.11 read them from the clients); they only imitate the usual shape - table name first, then stakes and game. Placeholders: {table} the table name as written in the hands, {stakes} '$0.05/$0.10', {stakesDash} '$0.05-$0.10', {currency} 'USD', {game} from 'games', {gameFile} from 'gameFiles', {hero}, {size} seats, {tid} tournament id, {tno} table number, {tname} tournament name, {gid} a per-table game id, {date} YYYYMMDD of the hand (UTC).

sources.header: SOURCED: the live client's header, docs/research/hh-formats/pokerstars.md section 2; Zoom and Home Game hands are left out (their tables are not ordinary windows).
sources.sizes: SOURCED: the cash table sizes in fixtures/samples/pokerstars (9-max 73 hands, 6-max 18, heads-up 2).
sources.tableNames: SOURCED: drawn from the corpus's own table names (for example 'Hygiea IV 40-100 bb').
sources.dealt: SOURCED: 'Dealt to <hero> [cards]' right after '*** HOLE CARDS ***' (the corpus hands that have a hero).
sources.title: INVENTED (unverified): '<table> - <stakes> - <game> - Logged In as <hero>'; to be replaced by the real title when R3.3 reads it.
sources.file: PARTLY SOURCED: 'HH<YYYYMMDD> <table name> - <stakes> - <game>.txt' is the client's own name (pokerstars.md section 12, 'HH20200618 lets gooooo - 50-100 - Play Money No Limit Hold'em.txt'); the money form of the stakes is INVENTED. One file per table and day. Tournament file name INVENTED.
sources.encoding: SOURCED: most real files start with a UTF-8 BOM and use LF (pokerstars.md section 12).
sources.separator: SOURCED: hands separated by two blank lines (fixtures/samples/pokerstars/27-cash-multi-hand-file-blank-line-separator.txt).
sources.window: INVENTED: a typical default table size.

sources.header: SOURCED: docs/research/hh-formats/winamax.md section 2 (cash games only; the corpus has no Winamax tournament hand, so tournaments are refused).
sources.sizes: SOURCED: the corpus's cash tables are 5-max (25 hands), heads-up (4) and 9-max (4); no 6-max.
sources.title: INVENTED (unverified).
sources.file: INVENTED: no real Winamax export name is known (winamax.md section 12); '<date>_<table>_real_<game>.txt' is a guess to verify.
sources.encoding: SOURCED: UTF-8 with BOM and LF in most corpus files (winamax.md section 12).
sources.separator: SOURCED: five blank lines between hands (winamax.md section 12, CashGame_MultipleHandsTests_10MultipleHands.txt). The corpus file's last hand has no line end at all; whether the client writes the separator before or after a hand is unknown - before would make a live file's last hand end without a line end (the watcher's settle time, R1.3).

sources.header: SOURCED: the current grammar ('era C', 'Hand #... - ' and 'Game Hand #... - ', docs/research/hh-formats/acr-wpn.md); the legacy 'Game started at:' eras are left out - a live client writes one grammar.
sources.sizes: SOURCED: the era-C cash hands in fixtures/samples/acr-wpn that the simulator can use: 6-max (1 hand) and 9-max (3); none heads-up. The same few hands repeat, each time with a fresh id, names, seats and time.
sources.tableNames: SOURCED: the corpus's table names ('Blitz Poker', 'Miramar (Cap)', ...).
sources.dealt: SOURCED: 'Dealt to <hero> [cards]' right after '*** HOLE CARDS ***' (era-C fixtures).
sources.title: INVENTED (unverified).
sources.file: PARTLY SOURCED: the fpdb fixtures keep fragments of WPN's own names ('HH20160621 G30997753', 'CASHID-TN-Miramar (Cap) GAMETYPE', 'SCHEDULEDID-TN-The Venom ... GAMETYPE'); the full shape is INVENTED around them.
sources.encoding: PARTLY SOURCED: era-C fixtures are plain ASCII/UTF-8 (acr-wpn.md section 12); older files are UTF-8 with BOM or UTF-16LE - use --encoding to write those.
sources.separator: PARTLY SOURCED: one blank line between hands in era A/B files (acr-wpn.md section 12); no multi-hand era-C file is in the corpus.
